theme.title: Around the League
theme.subtitle: Teams, stars and stories from across basketball
theme.recap: The best numbers come from all over basketball history. Which answer surprised you most?

questions.prompt: How many points per game did Tim Duncan average in the 1999 Finals?
questions.note: 27.4 points per game while winning Finals MVP.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: while averaging 27.4 points and fourteen rebounds with 2.4 assists and 2.2 blocks in the Finals

funFacts.text: Duncan was in his second NBA season alongside David Robinson in the Twin Towers pairing.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The 1998–99 season was the second season of the "Twin Towers" pairing

funFacts.text: San Antonio drafted Duncan after an injury-hit season and a fortunate draft lottery.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Spurs earned this draft pick through the draft lottery due to a 62-loss 1996–97 season

funFacts.text: The Knicks were an eighth seed when they reached the Finals, an extraordinary playoff run.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Knicks barely qualified for the playoffs and received the eighth and final seed

questions.prompt: In Hakeem Olajuwon's 1990 quadruple-double, how many shots did he block?
questions.note: Eleven rejections completed a remarkable four-category performance.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: 18 points, 16 rebounds, 11 blocks and 10 assists

funFacts.text: Hakeem's quadruple-double came in a comfortable Houston victory over Milwaukee.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: 120–94 win over the Milwaukee Bucks

funFacts.text: He led the entire NBA in blocked shots that season, averaging 4.6 a night.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: led the league in blocks by averaging 4.6 per game

funFacts.text: He also led the league in rebounds during that same remarkable defensive season.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: He won the NBA rebounding crown

questions.prompt: Manute Bol set the record for blocks in a quarter in December 1985. How many?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: 8 blocks in the first quarter, setting the NBA record, and 11 blocks in the first half, tying the NBA record

funFacts.text: Bol set his mark while playing for Washington in an overtime victory against the Milwaukee Bucks.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Washington Bullets  | December 12, 1985  | Milwaukee Bucks

funFacts.text: The rookie also reached a huge first-half swat total in the same game against Milwaukee.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: 11 blocks in the first half, tying the NBA record

funFacts.text: Bol later repeated the feat in a fourth quarter against Indiana during his Washington years.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: 8 blocks in the fourth quarter, tying the NBA record

questions.prompt: The 2003–04 Pistons were the first team to hold how many straight opponents under 70 points?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: They became the first team in NBA history to hold five consecutive opponents under 70 points

funFacts.text: Detroit's front office added Rasheed Wallace in a complicated trade at the deadline.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: for guard Mike James and forward Rasheed Wallace

funFacts.text: The Pistons had replaced Rick Carlisle with Larry Brown as head coach before the season.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: In his place, Dumars hired legendary coach Larry Brown

funFacts.text: Ben Wallace and Richard Hamilton were acquired through trades rather than drafted by Detroit.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: He landed defensive stalwart Ben Wallace and guard Richard Hamilton by trading established stars

questions.prompt: Down 3–2 to Durant's Thunder in 2016, how many points did Klay Thompson score in his legendary Game 6?
questions.context: Klay Thompson · Warriors at Thunder · 2016 playoffs
questions.note: 41 points, with a playoff-record barrage of threes to force a decider.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Klay Thompson, who scored a series-high 41 points and made an NBA playoff record 11 3s.

funFacts.text: Klay set a postseason record for made threes.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: made an NBA playoff record 11 3s

funFacts.text: The Warriors won on the road to force a deciding game.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Warriors won the game 108–101 and tied the series 3-3

funFacts.text: The Thunder had held a commanding series lead.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Thunder once again handed the Warriors a commanding 118–94 defeat to take a 3–1 series lead
